title: Rajkumar Hirani Finally Goes Streaming — and Hands His Own Son the Lead. 'Pritam And Pedro' Lands July 3.
excerpt: Bollywood's most beloved storyteller makes his OTT debut on JioHotstar with a Goa-set cybercrime comedy. Vir Hirani plays the hacker. Arshad Warsi plays the cop. And the Munna Bhai magic is quietly back in the room.
body:
There's a particular kind of nervousness that only a father directing his son for the first time can feel, and you can almost sense it humming under the **Pritam And Pedro** trailer. The man who gave us *Munna Bhai*, *3 Idiots*, *PK* and *Sanju* — the rare filmmaker whose name alone sells a ticket — has finally stepped onto streaming, and instead of playing it safe with a marquee star, **Rajkumar Hirani** has bet his first OTT project on the boy he raised.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU</youtube>

The boy, **Vir Hirani**, was last seen as a tiny ShortCircuit in *Lage Raho Munna Bhai* two decades ago, perched beside Arshad Warsi. Now he's the lead. And on Father's Day, Vir posted a cheeky note calling his dad the "man responsible for my birth and my employment." If you didn't already know this was a family affair, that line settled it.

**Pritam And Pedro** premieres on **JioHotstar** on July 3 — a Goa-set cybercrime comedy-drama that the makers describe, deliciously, as a world "where data meets danda, chaos meets confusion." That single phrase tells you everything about the tonal register: this is Hirani in his comfort zone, the place where slapstick and sincerity hold hands, where the villain is never quite a villain.

> "In Rajkumar Hirani's films, the villain is never a person; it is always the situation. You can never truly hate the villain in his films." — Vikrant Massey

**Vikrant Massey**, who plays the shadowy Martin, put his finger on exactly what makes a Hirani story land. People aren't wicked, they're cornered. Circumstances push them. It's a gentler moral universe than most thrillers allow, and it's the reason audiences have trusted this filmmaker for twenty-five years.

The premise is irresistibly Hirani: Vir plays **Pritam**, a tech-savvy hacker with a conscience that keeps getting in the way, and **Arshad Warsi** plays **Pedro**, a dogged police officer who still thinks the answer to every problem is a good chase. Throw them into a high-pressure kidnapping case that drags both men into the murky, fast-moving world of digital surveillance and cybercrime, and you have the clash the trailer leans into hardest — old-school police instinct versus a criminal landscape that lives entirely behind a screen.

The casting is a quiet flex. Beyond Warsi, Massey and Vir, the ensemble folds in **Boman Irani** and **Mona Singh** — Hirani regulars who feel like family by now. The series is directed by **Avinash Arun**, the cinematographer-turned-filmmaker behind *Killa*, *Three of Us* and *Paatal Lok*, which means the Goa backdrop won't just be postcard-pretty; it'll be looked at properly. Hirani co-wrote the story and screenplay with longtime collaborator **Abhijat Joshi** and Suyash Trivedi.

And then there's the music, which is where the nostalgia turns lethal. Lyricist **Swanand Kirkire** has reunited with Hirani to pen a retro melody composed by **Shantanu Moitra** and sung by **Shreya Ghoshal** — a combination engineered in a lab to make anyone over thirty go misty. "Retro songs have a certain innocence and lyrical simplicity that we don't often see anymore," Kirkire said of the track. "I wanted the lyrics to carry the fragrance of old Hindi cinema without becoming an imitation of it." With Ghoshal's voice on top, he added, "it felt complete."

For the Warsi faithful, the real pull is the reunion. His Circuit in the *Munna Bhai* films remains one of Hindi cinema's most quoted comic performances, and watching him slip back into a Hirani world — this time opposite his old director's grown son — carries a sweetness no marketing team could manufacture. At the trailer launch, Warsi couldn't resist ribbing the family, recalling how a young Vir once refused to give a shot until he'd been paid.

For the diaspora, the math is simple. **Pritam And Pedro** streams on **JioHotstar** from July 3, which means NRIs across the US, UK and Canada can watch the same week as Mumbai — no piracy, no waiting, no spoilers leaking through the family WhatsApp group before you've pressed play. (In the US, JioHotstar content typically routes through the Hotstar/Disney+ ecosystem; check your regional listing close to release.)

The stakes here are bigger than one show. If Hirani can carry his theatrical magic onto a streaming series — and launch a star in the process — it reshapes what India's most bankable directors do next. The web series stopped being a consolation prize a while ago. With *Pritam And Pedro*, it just got a Hirani stamp. Don't bet against the man who's never made a flop.
